Let \(r(U,W)=3-\dim(U\cap W)\). In this Grassmann graph, \(d(U,W)=r(U,W)\), so the possible distances are \(0,1,2,3\).

The distance matrices \(A_i\), where \((A_i)_{UW}=1\) iff \(d(U,W)=i\), form the Grassmann association scheme \(J_2(6,3)\). Its nontrivial eigenspaces have multiplicities
\[
62,\quad 588,\quad 744.
\]
For the adjacency matrix \(A_1\), the corresponding eigenvalues are
\[
35,\quad 5,\quad -7.
\]
Using the distance-regular recurrence with intersection array
\[
b_0=98,\ b_1=72,\ b_2=32,\qquad c_1=1,\ c_2=9,\ c_3=49,
\]
one obtains the eigenvalues of \(A_2,A_3\) on those same eigenspaces:
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
 & A_1 & A_2 & A_3\\ \hline
62 & 35 & 28 & -64\\
588 & 5 & -22 & 16\\
744 & -7 & 14 & -8
\end{array}
\]
Thus the metric matrix
\[
D_p=A_1+2^pA_2+3^pA_3
\]
has nontrivial eigenvalues
\[
\lambda_1(p)=35+28\cdot 2^p-64\cdot 3^p,
\]
\[
\lambda_2(p)=5-22\cdot 2^p+16\cdot 3^p,
\]
\[
\lambda_3(p)=-7+14\cdot 2^p-8\cdot 3^p.
\]

Negative type is exactly the condition that \(D_p\) is negative semidefinite on the zero-sum subspace, so all three \(\lambda_i(p)\le 0\). At \(p=0\), all three equal \(-1\). The first eigenvalue to reach \(0\) is
\[
\lambda_2(p)=5-22\cdot 2^p+16\cdot 3^p.
\]
This function is strictly increasing for \(p\ge 0\), since
\[
\lambda_2'(p)=16(\log 3)3^p-22(\log 2)2^p>0,
\]
and it changes sign between \(0\) and \(1\). Therefore
\[
\wp
\]
is the unique positive solution of
\[
16\cdot 3^p-22\cdot 2^p+5=0.
\]
Numerically,
\[
\wp\approx 0.270530819610378.
\]

At \(p=\wp\), only the eigenspace of multiplicity \(588\) has eigenvalue \(0\). Hence
\[
\dim E=588.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(\wp,\dim E\right)=\left(\text{the unique positive root of }16\cdot 3^p-22\cdot 2^p+5=0,\ 588\right)}.
\]
